blocks.content: The President shall, within two years from the commencement of this Constitution and thereafter at the expiration of every fifth year or at such earlier time as the President considers necessary, by order constitute a Finance Commission.

items: The recommendations made by the Finance Commission are purely advisory in nature and not binding on the Government.
Qualifications of the Chairman and members are laid down in the Finance Commission (Miscellaneous Provisions) Act, 1951.
Sub-clauses (bb) and (bc) of Article 280(3) mandate measures to augment the Consolidated Fund of a State to supplement resources of Panchayats and Municipalities.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 280 of the Indian Constitution provides for a quasi-judicial body known as the Finance Commission of India.
The Finance Commission is constituted by the President of India every fifth year, or at such earlier time as deemed necessary.
Parliament is authorized by law to determine the qualifications required for members of the Commission and the manner of their selection.
The primary mandate of the Commission is to recommend the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
It also recommends the principles governing grants-in-aid to the States out of the Consolidated Fund of India under Article 275.
